chart.summary: Engram is a local AI-maintained repository Cortex with compact bounded JSON snapshots, an offline local runtime, revision-safe mutations, task-focused retrieval, a persistent MCP interface, optional recoverable audit history, and separate explicit-Cortex retrieval indexes; it never scans, parses, or infers from source code.

areas.label: Cortex storage
areas.summary: The CLI persists a bounded compact JSON Cortex and exposes revision-safe read, replace, apply, validate, status, and atomic mutation locking. Lock metadata supports safe recovery only when a prior writer PID is definitively gone.

areas.label: Cerebellum
areas.summary: init installs the Cerebellum, which tells agents how to form and maintain the Cortex.

areas.label: Performance and protected agent evaluation
areas.summary: The repeatable storage benchmark measures direct and fresh-CLI Cortex latency. Eval v2 runs versioned agent tasks in disposable fixture copies, protects grading with external judges and whole-workspace diff enforcement, and emits auditable JSON/Markdown reports plus raw traces.

areas.label: Persistent MCP service
areas.summary: engram-mcp is a persistent stdio MCP server that exposes structured Cortex reads, safe mutations, validation, and history verification without fresh CLI startup per tool call.

areas.label: Audit and retrieval
areas.summary: Optional content-addressed history records safe mutations with recovery checkpoints every 50 events. A pending journal allows the next history check or mutation to reconcile an audit append interrupted after Cortex persistence; explicit Cortex roots can produce a separate derived search index without source scanning.

areas.label: Local runtime and task focus
areas.summary: init copies the dependency-free CLI/runtime into .engram/runtime so ordinary Cortex work is independent of npm and network state. focus returns a bounded, ranked slice of agent-authored entries, a diverse initial evidence queue, and a source-verification correctness gate for task navigation; it never opens source files.

areas.label: Automatic evidence
areas.summary: Successful Cortex CLI/MCP operations record locally in bounded NDJSON. focus records only operation metadata and UTF-8-derived Cortex-context sizing, never raw prompts, source snippets, evidence paths, or model output. `.engram/evidence.json` makes local-only storage, opt-out, and bounded retention explicit; evidence export and team bundles are deliberate redacted outputs. Activity and sizing estimates are never task-outcome measurements.

areas.label: Agent host connection
areas.summary: The dependency-free local runtime includes a persistent stdio MCP server. doctor verifies the Cortex, runtime, MCP entry point, Cerebellum, and evidence-report skill without changing configuration. mcp-config prints an absolute-path configuration snippet for Codex, Cursor, VS Code, or generic MCP hosts; it never writes user-level agent settings.

areas.label: Installed agent workflow skills
areas.summary: init installs a repository-local onboarding skill plus workflow, Cortex-maintenance, evidence-report, and protected-evaluation skills. Onboarding asks one choice—Orientation or Quick setup—then either gives a one-minute three-point introduction or skips directly to forming the first evidence-backed Cortex. The other skills direct ordinary work, reporting, and protected evaluation; none start a browser or server.

areas.label: Team handoff bundles
areas.summary: bundle produces an explicit JSON handoff containing a Cortex snapshot and revision, history verification, automatic-evidence summary, and stated limitations. It excludes raw evidence events, prompts, snippets, and model output; it is a sharing convenience rather than an access-control boundary.

workflows.label: Bootstrap
workflows.summary: README contains only a short agent handoff with the raw GitHub URL for onboarding, so it works before `.engram` exists. The remote onboarding skill offers Orientation or Quick setup; it runs init with an isolated npm cache when the local runtime is missing, then installs the repository-local skills/runtime and forms the first Cortex. init preserves any existing Cortex. Package smoke tests verify packed installation, initialization, and local-runtime validation.

workflows.label: Maintenance
workflows.summary: Agents read a fresh revision before mutations; stale or overlapping writes return explicit conflicts. Dead-writer locks are recovered safely, and pending audited mutations reconcile before the next mutation or history verification.

workflows.label: Benchmarking
workflows.summary: Run npm run bench to measure isolated temporary Cortex workloads without scanning or mutating source repositories.

workflows.label: Cross-repository retrieval
workflows.summary: A caller explicitly lists repository roots to build a derived Cortex index and searches that artifact; the indexer reads only Cortex snapshots.

workflows.label: Task navigation
workflows.summary: At investigation start, query focus with distinctive task terms, open only its bounded evidence paths first, and expand only when a requested conclusion remains unproven. Cortex keywords guide retrieval but never prove a claim. Complete the correctness gate—especially authorization/persistence/post-action tracing—then upsert verified recurring boundaries or test seams with 2–8 keywords.

workflows.label: Protected agent evaluation
workflows.summary: Validate fixtures and intentionally failing baselines with npm run eval -- --validate. A typed adapter writes a requested JSON artifact into a disposable workspace; external judges validate citations/functionality while whole-workspace diffs reject undeclared mutations. Reports retain raw traces plus suite, adapter, prompt, fixture, and judge hashes. Cortex learning uses a teacher-created Cortex and fresh control/treatment solvers with paired deltas.

workflows.label: Agent evidence reporting
workflows.summary: init installs the repository-local evidence-report skill beside the Cerebellum. An agent reads its bounded local evidence summary, answers the user's specific question as a polished, rendered, visually verified PDF, and returns a brief chat summary with the artifact. It separates activity/context-sizing estimates from measured task outcomes. If the skill or runtime is absent, the README prompt directs the agent to bootstrap Engram first.

workflows.label: Connect an AI host
workflows.summary: After init, run doctor. Generate a host-specific MCP snippet with mcp-config, add only the Engram server entry to the host configuration, then start a new agent session and verify it can call engram_read. The connection is explicit and local; setup never edits user configuration automatically.

workflows.label: Protected evaluation reporting
workflows.summary: For outcome claims, validate and run a fixed protected control/treatment suite with an explicit adapter and multiple repetitions. Container adapters are required for real comparisons; unsafe local adapters are development-only. Give the exact eval v2 report to the evidence-report skill so its visually verified PDF preserves hashes, trust level, model metadata, repetitions, and comparison boundaries.

workflows.label: Team handoff
workflows.summary: Review Cortex changes with code, use history for recoverability when needed, and create a deliberate bundle for another team or agent. CI validates tooling and packaging but reviewers must verify agent-authored Cortex claims against cited evidence.

workflows.label: Compatibility and upgrades
workflows.summary: Engram supports Node 20 and 22 in CI. init refreshes the local runtime and skills without replacing Cortex knowledge; migrate is a read-only format-status check. Any future format change requires a documented revision-safe migration and upgrade tests.

decisions.label: Agent-owned knowledge
decisions.summary: All repository understanding is authored and maintained by agents, not derived by Engram from code.

decisions.label: Compact JSON for agents
decisions.summary: The Cortex uses compact named-field JSON with hard AI working-set limits because it is directly reliable agent context; denser encodings and a Rust rewrite remain unjustified by the measured storage path.

decisions.label: Revisioned mutations
decisions.summary: All apply and replace operations require the read snapshot revision and use an exclusive local lock; this favors explicit agent recovery over silent last-write-wins data loss.

decisions.label: Self-contained installed runtime
decisions.summary: The bootstrap command may come from npx or a package install, but init must make normal Cortex operation self-contained in the target repository. This prevents npm-cache, registry, and GitHub-resolution failures from blocking agents after setup.

decisions.label: Evidence-bounded task protocol
decisions.summary: Focused retrieval is an initial evidence budget, not a source of truth: favor diverse relevant paths, avoid unrelated recursive instruction loading, and require source-backed conclusions. Maintain verified recurring discoveries as keyworded Cortex entries so future investigations start at durable anchors.

decisions.label: Protected evaluation boundary
decisions.summary: Agent output never determines its own score: judges execute outside the workspace, every undeclared mutation fails integrity, and local execution is labelled unsafe. For real comparisons, use a container adapter that mounts only the disposable workspace and defaults to no network; model/proxy configuration remains explicit adapter metadata.

decisions.label: Agent-native reporting
decisions.summary: Engram exposes local Cortex and evidence data to an AI agent through CLI and MCP rather than a browser dashboard. The agent reads the repository-local evidence-report skill and produces a rendered PDF tailored to the user's question; it must distinguish local activity and context-sizing estimates from measured outcomes.

conventions.label: Minimal docs
conventions.summary: README and docs stay concise; the Cerebellum contains the operative workflow.

conventions.label: Performance evidence
conventions.summary: Performance claims use the repeatable benchmark with p50/p95 measurements and distinguish in-process safe workflows from fresh CLI read-plus-apply latency.

conventions.label: Release verification
conventions.summary: CI runs syntax checks, unit tests, protected eval-fixture validation, and a packed-artifact smoke test on Node 20 and 22. Releases also document compatibility, read-only migration status, and the distinction between automatic evidence estimates and protected evaluation outcomes.

conventions.label: Honest evidence metrics
conventions.summary: UTF-8-size-derived focus reduction is an estimated Cortex-context reduction, not total task savings. Automatic evidence may show local activity, initial setup, time to first Cortex, and aggregate focus-sizing estimates; measured token, time, and success deltas require a protected paired evaluation.
